fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Devil As The Ultimate Boogeyman", "body": "Chance opens by pushing back on the wave of literalist Christianity moving through the truther scene, where Noah is a real man, the thousand year millennial reign has come and gone, and every problem gets blamed on Satan, Belial, Beelzebub, the Nephilim and the spirits of fallen angels. He argues this is the same product as the Gnostic prison planet, demiurge and simulation theory pitch. Every control system needs an ultimate boogeyman, because blame is what keeps people spending what he calls victim currency instead of taking responsibility for their own lives."}, {"title": "Original Sin And The Broken Self", "body": "The pair treat original sin as the load bearing lie of the whole structure. Chance describes it as convincing people they are intrinsically broken, that a tempter causes them to do bad things and that they have no real choice in the matter. Most people never say that out loud, but it is what the devil concept quietly installs in a culture. Dylan calls modern victimhood the cancer of society, noting how people now choose to be offended by a plain statement of preference, standards or a code of honor, and how coddling somebody in hard times helps nobody."}, {"title": "Language As Forensic Evidence Of Forgery", "body": "Dylan makes the case that scripture betrays itself through its own words. He asks why Paul would write to Romans in Greek to preach good news to Italians, comparing it to appealing to the British in Arabic. He points to terms like agion and agios carrying a martyrdom context alien to the Roman mind, arguing these passages cannot have been written when they are claimed to have been. Language is forensic, he says, because even a forgery leaves its fingerprints, and this is what exposes the third and fourth century takeover that severed the stories from nature."}, {"title": "Robert Taylor And The Beggarly Gospel", "body": "They continue their reading of Reverend Robert Taylor, a man they say was swept into the dustbin of history. The quoted passage calls the gospel peculiarly adapted for the poor, a beggarly gospel whose order of the day was to bring in the maimed, the halt and the blind and compel them to come in without ever asking their consent. Taylor calls it the morality necessary to keep the lower orders in subjection, and charges that those who thrive on it are too cowardly to defend it in open controversy against the infidels who challenge them."}, {"title": "Neutral Ground Between Creator And Destroyer", "body": "Both hosts insist this is not a Satanism pitch. Chance says they remain neutral, holding that everything scriptural is allegory for nature and the cycles created by the sun, so the symbolic identity of God and the devil is not an invitation to worship horns and a pitchfork. He traces the creator and destroyer schism to the Zoroastrian era and the split between Ahriman and his counterpart, and reads the devil's horns as the Hebrew qaran, radiance and light, the same rays and cornucopia symbolism found on old sculptures of Moses. Dylan adds that none of these Abrahamic systems are his culture."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Episode 6 of Inner Whirled continues our revival of the incredible Astronomico-Theological Lectures of the Rev. Robert Taylor, taking a deep dive into the details around the Devil in religious mythology. Our exploration encompasses the linguistic clues around this enigmatic figure, scriptural evidence for his true identity as an aspect of the Sun, how his titles and attributes mirror him to the savior archetype, what snakes have to do with it all, and much more. There's no better education out there to demystify the Devil, so bring your notebooks and enjoy!

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Savior And The Destroyer Are One Being", "body": "The members' half turns on a single claim read straight out of Taylor, that the destroyer and the savior were never two beings. Beelzebub and Apollyon are unpacked into Abaddon, which is broken down as Abba and Adon, father and lord, so the name Christians cry out is the same name they curse. The hundredth Psalm is offered as the plain version of it, he can create and he can destroy. Paul's language about descending into the lower parts of the earth and ascending far above all heavens then becomes one figure making an annual round, the devil turning into Christ at the vernal equinox and back again."}, {"title": "Opposition Is Astronomy And Not Hostility", "body": "Taylor's mechanism gets laid out in full. As the sun passes through the twelve signs, whichever sign it occupies is the supreme God for that season and the directly opposite sign is the accuser, the adversary, the devil, so every sign takes both parts in its turn. The scorpion in the gates of hell is named as the genius of October, reigning over the five months from October to February before the Lamb of God arrives in March. Chance closes the episode on the same point, that the devil is never described with words of hostility and that opposition here is an astronomical signifier."}, {"title": "The Serpent As Wisdom Creator And Savior", "body": "A long stretch rebuilds the serpent of Genesis as the emblem of the creator rather than the villain. Irenaeus is cited calling the heretical sects Ophites after the snake they revered, and Sophia is noted to carry Ophis inside it. The Hebrew arum is shown to mean both crafty and naked, tying the snake to wisdom and to the erotic spark that kept the species going. Buddha's serpent hood, the cobra renewing itself by shedding its skin, Naga and nahash as serpent and shining one, and the brazen Nehushtan lifted on a pole all land on the same reading."}, {"title": "Language And Artifacts As The Forensic Record", "body": "Dylan spends the back half showing how he actually works, through letters and objects rather than argument. Asher is spelled out and carried into Aesir, Acer and Caesar, and Asgard becomes the boundary of the sun. Isaiah is transliterated back to a root meaning savior, and Yeshua reduces to the same letters. A Phoenician zeta on a vase and the IU primus atar on old coins are traced into Zeus and Jupiter, the Irish lamh, meaning hand, is folded into the lamb of God, and the word for priest turns out to match the word for a corpse. His standing claim is that all of it is cited and sourced."}, {"title": "The Devil As Idol And What Replaces It", "body": "Running underneath the scholarship is an argument about what belief in a literal devil actually does. Higgins is quoted saying that in these days, certainly, no devil means no priests, and Chance extends it, calling the devil an idol that was never literal to the old system, a false scapegoat made out of a misunderstood allegory that gets worshipped, feared and blamed in turn. The same charge falls on any promise of a future utopia, religious or political, for degrading the present moment. Chance ends by claiming the astrotheological reading is the only interpretation demonstrable with evidence and that the rest is inference and opinion."}]

fields.Plus Quotes JSON: [{"text": "Always degrading the present moment for a future promise when there's no reason to believe that. That's totally a promise of the devil.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "I've stepped away from any type of interpretation of Revelation once I found out so much of it was made up by Erasmus.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "That old serpent, the devil, saved humanity by getting Adam and Eve to bone.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "The devil is an idol that was never literal to the old system, probably, but symbolic of the destructive power necessary for creation.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "The snake is just propelled by his strength and life and being himself, just like the cosmos.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "I'm going in the historical record. I'm looking at artifacts. I'm not just sitting here philosophizing about the findings.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "So the priests were connected to the navigators, and they were going from place to place long before the average person knew about it.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "The astrotheological interpretation is the only one that is demonstrable with evidence in an airtight way. All the other interpretations are opinion.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "So in terms of the mercantile empire, in this sign you will conquer, in this sign you will purchase.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Once you increase your knowledge and learn how to do this work and read the alphabets, you'll see it like we see it.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}]
